descriptor.scene: THE MANAGER IS INSIDE HIS MACHINE AND JUNE IS NOT. She never enters the factory and he never steps out onto her porch; no figure crosses between them. One frame, two places, joined only by light. At the LEFT of the frame, set into the cream wall of the glowing machine, a tall warm OVAL OPENING like a window of daylight: inside it, painted as a real place, a wooden porch in warm afternoon sun, and June standing there from the waist up, clear and the subject of her half, speaking a voice note into a plain modern smartphone held close to her mouth, her other hand resting lightly over her heart. Her afternoon light spills a little way onto the factory floor. From that opening a SMALL FLOATING VOICE-NOTE SHAPE drifts across the middle of the frame toward the right: a soft rounded glowing bubble carrying one simple little waveform, and it is the only thing that travels between the two places. At the RIGHT of the frame the manager stands on his low wooden platform inside the machine, from the waist up, clear and the subject of his half, head tilted UP toward the drifting voice note, whole body attentive, both mitten arms relaxed. He is a hand-span glowing figure in his own place and she is a full-grown woman in hers; the oval opening is what keeps the two scales honest. Warm afternoon gold on her side, warm plum and cream on his, and the factory behind him is quiet and softly out of focus.
descriptor._caption: A voice note arrives, the way work always arrives. June, on her porch: Theo starts school on Monday, and he is scared of the big doors. The manager listens twice. Listening is the part of the job only he can do.

eyeglasses on June, on her face, pushed up on her head or on a cord
June's hair worn down or cut short; it is a low silver bun at the nape
a hard-edged panel border, gutter or split-screen line between the two places
